newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares firm 0.8 pct ahead of censure motion.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares firm 0.8 pct ahead of censure motion.

text.p: Istanbul shares firmed in selective and range-bound trade on Tuesday, ahead of a censure motion debate against the Islamist-led coalition government which began in parliament, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,641, up 13 points, or 0.8 percent from Monday, but down from an early high of 1,652. Trade volume leapt to 30.21 trillion lira from Monday's 20.62 trillion.
"Trade became dull in the afternoon with selective activity focusing largely state-owned and finance shares. The index faced resistance at 1,650," said Zeki Direk from Eczacibasi securities.
Brokers said the market would face resistance at 1,700, the all-time high closing reached on January 27, even if the vote results were positive.
Parliament began its debate on the censure motion filed by two leftist parties after the market closed.
"The market will set direction from the result of the vote," said dealer Koray Cervatoglu.
The index gained 3.86 percent last week amid relief after parliament rejected sending Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller to the Supreme Court in three corruption charge votes.
The main opposition conservative Motherland Party put forward another censure motion, expected to be heard next week.

Of the 237 shares traded, 99 advanced, 97 declined and 41 were steady. The IMKB Industrial edged up 0.12 percent to 1,678, the IMKB Services firmed 0.88 percent to 1,488 and the IMKB Financial rose 1.6 percent to 1,713.
Actives were led by largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli which was unchanged at 21,750 lira. It made up about nine percent of the total turnover.
